adventure.title: Bonfire at Golden Gardens
adventure.description: One of the last legal beach-fire beaches in the city — claim a pit at Golden Gardens, feed it driftwood-adjacent fuel from home, and watch the sun drop behind the Olympics.
adventure.bonus: Stay until the fire is coals and the ferry lights are the brightest thing on the water.

adventure.title: Bill Speidel's Underground Tour
adventure.description: Since 1965 this irreverent tour has led people through the buried storefronts beneath Pioneer Square — the actual 1889 city, entombed when Seattle rebuilt itself one story up.
adventure.bonus: Ask your guide the one question the script doesn't cover — they always know more.

adventure.title: Discovery Park to the West Point Lighthouse
adventure.description: Seattle's largest park drops from meadow bluffs through forest to a working 1881 lighthouse on a driftwood beach — Sound on three sides, Rainier floating to the south, city nowhere in sight.
adventure.bonus: Touch the lighthouse fence, then find a full sand dollar on the walk back.

adventure.title: Bouldering at Stone Gardens Gym, Ballard
adventure.description: Stone Gardens has been Ballard's climbing institution since 1991, and the bouldering cave draws a local crowd serious enough to make every send feel earned.
adventure.bonus: Ask a stranger in the cave to beta you on a V4 or higher, then actually attempt it on the spot.

adventure.title: Raft the Skykomish Whitewater
adventure.description: The Skykomish's Index-to-Baring stretch serves up Class III–IV rapids through a granite canyon 90 minutes from Capitol Hill — book with one of the long-running guide outfits and hold on.
adventure.bonus: Run the Boulder Drop rapid without bracing once — arms out, let the river do it.

adventure.title: Paraglide off Tiger Mountain with Seattle Paragliding
adventure.description: Tiger Mountain's west-facing launch is 30 minutes from downtown — Seattle Paragliding's tandem flights soar you over the Issaquah Alps until the skyline looks like a toy.
adventure.bonus: Ask your pilot to do a 360-degree spiral and keep your eyes open the whole way through.

adventure.title: Climb the Rattlesnake Ledge Loop
adventure.description: Rattlesnake Ledge is the most climbed viewpoint in Washington for a reason — four miles round trip to a bare granite shelf with a straight-shot view down Rattlesnake Lake to Mount Rainier.
adventure.bonus: Scramble past the first ledge to the uppermost outcrop and eat your lunch sitting as close to the edge as you dare.

adventure.title: Explore the Burke-Gilman Trail by Bike
adventure.description: Seattle's 18-mile paved rail-trail stitches the University District to Kenmore along Lake Washington, passing breweries, boat launches, and beaches nearly the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Stop at Matthews Beach Park, ditch your bike, and jump into Lake Washington from the dock.

adventure.title: Scramble the Twin Falls Trail in Olallie State Park
adventure.description: Twin Falls drops 150 feet through old-growth cedar gorge just 30 miles from downtown, and the suspension bridge puts you right in the spray.
adventure.bonus: Cross the upper suspension bridge, stop in the middle, and sit down with your legs dangling over the edge for a full 60 seconds.

adventure.title: Ride the Bainbridge Island Ferry at Sunset
adventure.description: The Washington State Ferry crossing to Bainbridge Island delivers a moving panorama of the Olympic Mountains and downtown skyline that no rooftop bar can match.
adventure.bonus: Stand at the stern as Seattle shrinks away and stay there the full 35-minute crossing without checking your phone.

adventure.title: Hike to the Summit of Mount Si
adventure.description: The 8-mile round trip to the rocky summit of Mount Si is the Eastside's defining grunt, rewarding you with a wall of Cascades and the entire Snoqualmie Valley below.
adventure.bonus: Touch the haybale on the summit and take a photo with zero other people in the frame.

adventure.title: Kayak the Lake Union Houseboats
adventure.description: Paddling past Seattle's iconic floating homes on Lake Union puts you inside the city's most cinematic neighborhood from water level.
adventure.bonus: Drift close enough to a houseboat to read the name on the mailbox, then shout a compliment to anyone you see on their deck.

active.title: Beach Volleyball at Alki
active.description: West Seattle's beach strip runs pickup volleyball all summer with the downtown skyline across Elliott Bay — the closest Seattle gets to California, and it knows it.
active.bonus: Play until sunset, then walk the strip for fish and chips at Spud.

active.title: Loop Green Lake with the Regulars
active.description: The 2.8-mile path around Green Lake is Seattle's communal treadmill — strollers, rollerbladers, crew teams on the water, and eagles in the cottonwoods, every single day of the year.
active.bonus: Two laps — one easy, one at a pace you would not admit to.

active.title: Snowshoe the Franklin Falls Trail to Snoqualmie Pass Backcountry
active.description: The trailhead 45 minutes east of Seattle opens up into old-growth snow country where Franklin Falls freezes solid and the backcountry silence is absolute.
active.bonus: Touch the frozen waterfall with your bare hand and hold it there for 10 seconds — no gloves for the dare.

active.title: Walk the Cheshiahud Lake Union Loop
active.description: This 6.2-mile waterfront loop around Lake Union threads houseboats, boatyards, Eastlake cafés, and the South Lake Union waterfront into one continuous urban walk.
active.bonus: Stop at a random houseboat dock and strike up a conversation with whoever's outside — ask how long they've lived on the water.

active.title: Bike the Centennial Trail from Snohomish to Arlington
active.description: This 30-mile paved rail-trail cuts through old farmland and riverside forest north of Seattle — flat, fast, and genuinely removed from the city.
active.bonus: Ride the full 30-mile stretch one way and arrange a pickup — no turning back at the halfway point.

active.title: Trail Run the Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park
active.description: Nearly forty miles of forested trails inside King County's largest wildland park deliver genuine wilderness feel without leaving the city's orbit.
active.bonus: Find the Coal Creek Trail sign and run the full loop without stopping to walk — even the muddy switchbacks.

active.title: Ski a Powder Day at Crystal Mountain Resort
active.description: Washington's biggest ski area sits 76 miles southeast of Seattle and rewards the early alarm with 2,600 vertical feet of Cascade powder on uncrowded weekday runs.
active.bonus: Ski at least one double-black run you've never done before — no sidestepping, no traversing out.

active.title: Cold Plunge at Madison Park Beach
active.description: Madison Park's neighborhood beach on Lake Washington is Seattle's most civilized cold-water ritual — plunge, gasp, recover on the grassy bluff, repeat, then walk to coffee.
active.bonus: Get in past your shoulders — no tiptoeing — and stay for a full 60 seconds before you're allowed out.

active.title: Sunrise Hike to Poo Poo Point, Issaquah
active.description: The meadow launch site above Issaquah delivers a paraglider's-eye panorama of the Cascades at first light, even if you're just watching.
active.bonus: Stay until you watch at least one paraglider launch off the edge — then count how many seconds before they catch the thermal.

active.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard on Green Lake
active.description: Rent a board from Greenlake Boat Rentals and paddle the loop of Seattle's most beloved urban lake — it's deceptively meditative once you find your balance.
active.bonus: Paddle to the center of the lake, sit down on your board, and float in silence for five minutes without paddling anywhere.

active.title: Run the Myrtle Edwards Park Trail
active.description: This 1.25-mile waterfront trail hugging Elliott Bay gives you unobstructed views of the Olympics and the container port — best run in the city, full stop.
active.bonus: Run to the end of the fishing pier, stop, and watch the water for two full minutes before turning back.

active.title: Open-Water Swim at Seward Park
active.description: Seward Park's old-growth peninsula on Lake Washington has a calm swim beach with lifeguards in summer and cold, clear water that makes every stroke feel like a reset.
active.bonus: Swim out to the far swim buoy, tread water for 60 seconds facing the Mount Rainier horizon, then race yourself back to shore.

social.title: Catch a Show at the Showbox
social.description: Open since 1939 across from Pike Place, the Showbox's sprung dance floor has held everyone from Duke Ellington to Pearl Jam — the room every Seattle band dreams of headlining.
social.bonus: Get to the rail for the opener and give them the crowd they deserve.

social.title: Pinball and a Corn Dog at Shorty's
social.description: Belltown's clown-themed pinball dive has poured cheap drinks and served corn dogs under carnival lights since 1997 — a perfect, deeply weird Seattle institution.
social.bonus: Put your initials on at least one machine's high-score board — any letters that fit.

social.title: Private Room Karaoke at Rock Box
social.description: Capitol Hill's Japanese-style karaoke den rents dim, neon-trimmed private rooms with a deep bilingual songbook and drink service that keeps courage topped up.
social.bonus: Everyone in the room sings at least one solo — no duet hiding.

social.title: Catch a Mariners Day Game at T-Mobile Park
social.description: A sunny afternoon in the lower bowl at T-Mobile Park — with a Dungeness crab sandwich from the Edgar's Cantina concourse — is peak Seattle summer.
social.bonus: Start a chant in your section — it has to spread to at least three rows before the inning ends.

social.title: Ethiopian Feast at Jebena Café, Roosevelt
social.description: This Roosevelt neighborhood gem does a communal injera spread that turns lunch into a two-hour table event — order the combination platter and eat with your hands.
social.bonus: Order a traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony alongside your meal and stay for all three rounds — no skipping the third cup.

social.title: Steak Night at Bateau, Capitol Hill
social.description: Renée Erickson's Capitol Hill steakhouse dry-ages whole animals in-house and lists cuts on a chalkboard that changes as they sell — quiet confidence that makes a Tuesday feel like an occasion.
social.bonus: Order the butcher's cut — whatever they're featuring that night — and ask the server to explain exactly where on the animal it came from.

social.title: Afternoon Beer at Fremont Brewing Outdoor Beer Garden
social.description: Fremont Brewing's Urban Beer Garden has been a neighborhood anchor since 2009 — picnic tables, no-frills pours, dogs welcome, and zero pretense.
social.bonus: Sit at a communal table with strangers and get a beer recommendation from someone who's clearly a regular.

social.title: Drinks at Zig Zag Café, Pike Place Market
social.description: One of the most respected cocktail bars in the country hides beneath Pike Place Market and has been quietly converting skeptics since 1999.
social.bonus: Order nothing off the menu — give the bartender a single flavor word and let them build something from scratch.

social.title: Sunday Brunch at Glo's, Capitol Hill
social.description: This tiny, cash-only counter spot on 15th Avenue has served legendary eggs Benedict and pancakes since the 1980s — the line outside is part of the ritual.
social.bonus: Make friends with the couple next to you in line and offer to share a table — then actually do it.

social.title: Sunday Afternoon at Zeitgeist Coffee, Pioneer Square
social.description: Pioneer Square's most characterful café draws artists, architects, and old-school Seattleites into a high-ceilinged brick room that feels like the city's living room.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with a stranger at the communal table and find out what they're working on — genuinely ask a follow-up question.

social.title: Live Music at The Crocodile, Belltown
social.description: The club where Nirvana, Pearl Jam, and Mudhoney cemented grunge's legacy in the '90s still books the most exciting emerging acts in the Pacific Northwest.
social.bonus: Get to the floor before the headliner and introduce yourself to one person standing alone — find out what else they've seen here.

social.title: Sunday Morning at Ballard Farmers Market
social.description: Ballard Farmers Market runs year-round on Sunday mornings and is the market Seattle locals actually shop at — no fish-throwing theatrics, just honest PNW produce, bread, and oysters.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with a vendor, learn one thing about how they grow or make their product, and buy something you've never cooked before.

chill.title: Coffee and a Book at Lighthouse Roasters, Fremont
chill.description: Fremont's wood-fired roaster has pulled no-nonsense espresso in the same corner house since the early nineties — a quiet reading den that rewards lingering.
chill.bonus: Leave the phone in your pocket for the entire visit — order, sit, and finish at least 30 pages before you look at it again.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Wing Luke Museum, International District
chill.description: The Wing Luke has told the Asian Pacific American story since 1967, and its immersive, community-led exhibitions in the International District hit differently than any mainstream museum.
chill.bonus: Find the historic hotel room installation and spend at least 10 minutes inside it — alone, phone away.

chill.title: Explore the Museum of Flight, Boeing Field
chill.description: The largest private air and space museum in the world sits at Boeing Field and lets you walk through a Concorde, a 747, and a Space Shuttle trainer in a single afternoon.
chill.bonus: Find the original Boeing Red Barn and locate the year the company was founded stamped somewhere inside the building.

chill.title: Browse Twice Sold Tales, Capitol Hill
chill.description: This eccentric used bookshop stuffed floor-to-ceiling with cats and paperbacks has been a Capitol Hill institution since 1984 — it has no system and that's the point.
chill.bonus: Buy a book you know nothing about based only on its first sentence — no reading the back cover.

chill.title: Spend a Morning at Washington Park Arboretum
chill.description: This 230-acre living museum along the Montlake waterway has been maturing since 1934 — peak Japanese Garden season turns it into something otherworldly.
chill.bonus: Find a tree older than you by at least 50 years, sit underneath it, and read something — no scrolling.

chill.title: Visit the Chihuly Garden and Glass
chill.description: Dale Chihuly's glass universe sprawls across the Seattle Center in a permanent installation that transforms light into something you can't stop staring at.
chill.bonus: Find the installation where the ceiling meets the Space Needle — frame a photo where both overlap perfectly.

chill.title: Stroll the Olympic Sculpture Park at Dusk
chill.description: SAM's free waterfront park puts monumental sculpture against Puget Sound and the Olympics in a setting that makes fine art feel completely effortless.
chill.bonus: Touch every sculpture you're legally allowed to touch and photograph the most unexpected texture you find.

chill.title: Coffee at Victrola Coffee Roasters, Capitol Hill
chill.description: Seattle's most beloved independent roaster has been at the center of Capitol Hill's creative life since 2000 — slow down, order a pour-over, and stay a while.
chill.bonus: Order a single-origin you've never heard of and ask the barista exactly where the farm is — look it up on a map.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Seattle Art Museum
chill.description: SAM's permanent collection punches well above a city this size — the Northwest Coast Native art wing alone is worth the price of admission.
chill.bonus: Find one piece that genuinely unsettles you and sit with it for five full minutes — no phone.

chill.title: Wander Volunteer Park, Capitol Hill
chill.description: This 1876-era Olmsted-designed park holds a Victorian conservatory, a black sun sculpture, and sweeping views of the Olympics from its water tower.
chill.bonus: Climb the water tower and identify three mountain peaks on the horizon before you come back down.

chill.title: Sunset at Gasworks Park
chill.description: The rusting industrial towers of Gasworks Park on the north shore of Lake Union frame a downtown skyline at golden hour that's been Seattle's unofficial screensaver for 50 years.
chill.bonus: Climb to the top of the grassy kite hill and stay seated until the last sliver of sun drops below the Olympics.

chill.title: Read the Afternoon Away at Elliott Bay Book Company
chill.description: Elliott Bay Book Company's Capitol Hill warren of cedar shelves and hand-written staff notes has been the city's literary conscience since 1973.
chill.bonus: Buy a book chosen entirely by a staff recommendation card — no googling the author first.

foodie.title: Lunch at Salumi Artisan Cured Meats, Pioneer Square
foodie.description: Armandino Batali's legendary cured meat shop has been feeding Pioneer Square since 1999 — the muffuletta and lamb prosciutto are worth every minute of the line.
foodie.bonus: Strike up a conversation with whoever is in line next to you — ask them what they always order and then get that exact thing.

foodie.title: Cocktails at Canon, Capitol Hill
foodie.description: One of the most awarded whiskey bars in the country holds over 4,000 spirits — this is where serious drinkers come to get schooled.
foodie.bonus: Tell the bartender your mood, not your usual drink, and let them build you something from scratch — no vetoing ingredients.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Harbor City Restaurant, International District
foodie.description: Old-school Hong Kong–style cart service in the ID where har gow, turnip cake, and sticky rice in lotus leaf come fast and cheap.
foodie.bonus: Flag down every cart that passes and try at least one dish you can't identify — no asking, just pointing.

foodie.title: Pizza at Delancey, Ballard
foodie.description: Brandon Pettit's wood-fired pies have been the gold standard of Seattle pizza since 2009 — thin, blistered, and absolutely worth the wait.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the bar and watch the oven — ask the cook what tonight's special rotation is before you order.

foodie.title: Pho at Pho Bắc Súp Shop, Little Saigon
foodie.description: Third-generation family pho in the heart of Seattle's Vietnamese neighborhood — the broth is clear, complex, and deeply honest.
foodie.bonus: Eat your pho with no condiments added — taste the broth as intended before you reach for the hoisin.

foodie.title: Happy Hour at The Walrus and the Carpenter, Ballard
foodie.description: James Beard–recognized raw bar where briny Shigoku oysters and a tight natural wine list make Tuesday feel like a celebration.
foodie.bonus: Order an oyster you've never tried before and ask your server to describe exactly where it was harvested — then remember the name.

foodie.title: Ramen at Kizuki Ramen, University Village
foodie.description: Rich Hakata-style tonkotsu simmered for hours hits different on a grey Seattle afternoon — the University Village room is the reliable fix.
foodie.bonus: Order the spicy miso upgrade and challenge your table to finish the broth completely — no leaving a drop.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Café Besalu, Ballard
foodie.description: This tiny French pastry shop in Ballard produces croissants and galettes that rival anything you'd find in Paris — arrive early or miss out.
foodie.bonus: Get the last croissant of the batch — ask the baker when the next tray comes out and time your order perfectly.

foodie.title: Dinner at Canlis
foodie.description: Seattle's most iconic fine-dining room floats above Lake Union with mid-century bones, impeccable service, and a menu that earns every penny.
foodie.bonus: Order the tableside-prepared dish and strike up a real conversation with your captain server about the restaurant's 70-year history.

foodie.title: Breakfast at The Crumpet Shop, Pike Place Market
foodie.description: Open since 1976, The Crumpet Shop bakes its rounds to order and serves them with the kind of toppings — lemon curd, smoked salmon, local honey — that make Pike Place feel earned rather than toured.
foodie.bonus: Ask the staff what their personal favorite topping combination is and order exactly that.

foodie.title: Omakase at Shiro's Sushi, Belltown
foodie.description: Shiro Kashiba opened this Belltown counter in 1994 and the omakase remains the purest expression of Edomae sushi in the Pacific Northwest, full stop.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter, make eye contact with the chef, and ask them to choose one piece they're most proud of tonight.

foodie.title: Lunch at Paseo Caribbean Restaurant, Fremont
foodie.description: Paseo's Cuban roast sandwich — slow-cooked pork shoulder, pickled jalapeños, aioli, crusty bread — is the sandwich every Seattle local swears is worth the inevitable line.
foodie.bonus: Order without looking at the menu and eat the whole thing standing outside on the sidewalk.
